headline: Claude Code 2.1.325 puts sandboxed Bash through normal permissions by default
body: Anthropic released Claude Code 2.1.325 with a change to sandboxed Bash: commands now follow the normal permission flow by default. Users who want the previous no-prompt behavior can set sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed to true. The release also fixes a security issue in decoding zstd-compressed responses and gaps in Bash permission checks. Scheduled tasks and /loop now ask before running a skill that declares allowed-tools or hooks unless the skill is allowed explicitly.
why: Judgment: The permission-default change can interrupt unattended workflows. The release pairs it with fixes for command-approval gaps, so teams have an operational reason to review settings rather than treat this as a routine interface update.
watch: These are vendor release-note claims, not an independent security audit. Normal permission flow does not mean every command always prompts: existing rules still matter. No-prompt sandbox execution remains configurable. The notes do not state exploitation, severity scores or affected-version ranges. The release also changes other permission and plugin behavior; teams should test existing unattended workflows.

wrong_if: The default change is reverted or later release notes materially narrow which workflows it affects.

headline: DeepMind opens PARDIG precipitation and SatWeave satellite datasets, with historical archives and live feeds
body: Google DeepMind released public access to PARDIG and SatWeave, two datasets used behind WeatherNext 3. PARDIG provides AI-generated global precipitation estimates at roughly 10-kilometer spatial and 15-minute temporal resolution. SatWeave harmonizes geostationary satellite imagery into a global mosaic. Historical archives and continuing feeds are available through Google Cloud Storage; PARDIG historical catalogs are also available through Earth Engine.
why: Judgment: Open access can let researchers build weather, hydrology and climate applications without rebuilding these observation-processing pipelines.
watch: Dataset access, not a new forecast-model launch. PARDIG is experimental, not official observations or warnings, and must not be the sole source for safety decisions. Its 15-minute resolution is not arrival frequency: Cloud Storage updates in six-hour batches with ~2-8 hours effective latency. Guides list CC BY 4.0 and authenticated Google Cloud access without a request form. The dataset license does not establish that all cloud usage is cost-free. Performance claims are developer-reported, not independently verified here.
watch_next: Independent dataset validation, feed continuity and downstream weather and hydrology applications.
wrong_if: Coverage gaps, latency or experimental-data limits prevent useful downstream models.
likely_reaction: Muted (next-session judgment): open data supports research, but experimental status and multi-hour latency constrain operational use.

headline: Wolters Kluwer agrees up to $100 million AgileMD deal, with $40 million upfront and performance-linked balance

The deal comprises $40 million upfront and deferred consideration tied to performance targets. AgileMD provides clinical pathways embedded in electronic health-record workflows and the eCART clinical surveillance engine, which Wolters Kluwer describes as FDA-cleared. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027 or sooner, subject to conditions and government approvals.

watch: The deal is not completed. The full $100 million is not guaranteed consideration: the balance above $40 million depends on performance targets. Wolters Kluwer expects AgileMD to reach $7 million annual recurring revenue by year-end 2026 and says the acquisition should have an immaterial impact on adjusted earnings. Those are company forecasts. FDA clearance is attributed to the company and is not a claim that this acquisition or every AI feature is regulator-approved.

headline: SEC proposes narrower executive-pay disclosure and higher perks threshold; rules are not adopted
body: The US SEC proposed changes to Item 402 of Regulation S-K that would generally reduce named executive officers from five or more to the principal executive and financial officers. The proposal raises the minimum aggregate perquisites reporting threshold from $10,000 to $150,000, replaces four primary compensation tables with three new tables, and changes pay-versus-performance reporting. It would also limit median-employee calculations for pay ratios to US full-time workers and reset that determination every five years.
why: Judgment: If adopted, the proposal would change both the scope and comparability of executive-compensation information available to investors while giving companies more reporting flexibility.
watch: These are proposed amendments, not operative rules. The public-comment window is 60 days after publication of the proposing release in the Federal Register, not 60 days from the press release. The SEC says the changes aim to retain material information and reduce burdens; the effect on investor visibility is contested. The underlying mechanics of company clawback processes would remain unchanged under the proposal. No final effective date is established.

headline: Warburg Pincus agrees up to Rs 1,663 crore purchase of promoters' 38.51% in Pricol Autotech after demerger

Default offline configuration uses two CUDA GPUs and dequantizes the FP8 release. Dedicated serving branches provide optimized FP8 execution and streaming. This card concerns the quantized overlay, not the first Duo model/paper launch. No independent latency or quality benefit is established.

headline: India October goods exports rise 45.06% to $49.47 billion; goods trade deficit is $39.88 billion
body: Commerce Ministry provisional data show October merchandise exports of $49.47 billion, up 45.06% year on year, and imports of $89.35 billion, up 16.51%. The goods trade deficit was $39.88 billion, below $42.58 billion in October 2025. April-October merchandise exports rose 21.96% to $309.06 billion. These are goods-only figures, not the combined goods-and-services trade balance.
why: Judgment: Strong export growth coexists with a large goods import bill. The year-on-year goods deficit narrowed, so a claim that the deficit widened needs a clearly specified different comparison period.
watch: The official tables label October figures provisional and exports include re-exports. The owning release separately estimates combined goods-and-services exports at $89.99 billion and imports at $110.07 billion; services estimates and the combined balance should not be substituted for goods-only totals. Figures may be revised.

headline: India notifies IFSC commodity trading contracts as financial products, effective on gazette publication
body: The Finance Ministry notified commodity trading contracts as financial products under the IFSCA Act through S.O. 6196(E), dated November 13. A contract is one under which an IFSC unit trades a commodity with another party. The notification takes effect on publication in the Official Gazette. Commodities are goods capable of being delivered and traded, excluding actionable claims, money, currency and securities; CITES-listed species or specimens; and items specified by the Central Government under Special Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies (SCOMET).
why: Judgment: The classification is a concrete regulatory step for commodity trading through IFSC units. It is not evidence that a new trading platform is operational or that trading volumes have moved to GIFT City.
watch: The notification establishes a product classification and its exclusions. It does not itself announce a platform launch, trading volumes, tax concessions or blanket permission for every commodity or activity. Further operating rules and implementation are the next checks.

headline: llama.cpp and ggml reach v1.0.0 with explicit API compatibility rules and deprecated API removal
body: ggml-org released llama.cpp v1.0.0 and ggml v1.0.0, formalizing versioning rules for downstream developers: public C API breaking changes require major-version bumps, backward-compatible features use minor bumps, and bug fixes without API changes use patch bumps. The llama.cpp release removes 35 deprecated functions and promotes the NextN speculative-decoding interface into the public header. It also adds FP8 KV caches, a host-memory mixture-of-experts cache with a configurable CPU share, and an OpenAI-compatible speech-generation endpoint.
why: Judgment: A visible compatibility contract matters for applications built on local inference libraries. The first major-version milestone also requires migration work where downstream projects still use removed interfaces.
watch: Version 1.0 does not mean every future release is backward compatible: the project explicitly reserves major bumps for public API breaks. Existing integrations using deprecated functions need review. These are inference-library changes, not the release of a new foundation model, and the sources do not establish a universal speed or memory improvement.

headline: Claude Code 2.1.323 adds experimental opt-in Code Mode for JavaScript-based tool calls

The release notes also describe an organization-level option to turn it off. Plugin authors can now declare a supported Claude Code version range in plugin.json; incompatible plugins are not installed, updated or loaded. The release also adds TypeScript-hook type checking to plugin validation, with findings treated as warnings unless strict validation is used.

watch: Code Mode is experimental and opt-in, not a default rollout. This card concerns the Claude Code 2.1.323 release, not a new foundation model or a new Anthropic API feature. The release notes do not establish independent performance or cost gains.

headline: Mirendil announces $1 billion Series A to expand AI research models and agents
body: Mirendil announced a $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with participation from Google and other investors. The company is building models and tools for AI research and development. It says its Mirendil-Base coding model was pretrained by one researcher working with agents in 3.5 months using less than $10 million in compute, then post-trained into Fern with up to 10 million tokens of context. Lor, its platform for agents that write code and run experiments over multiple days, remains in private beta.
why: Judgment: The financing puts substantial capital behind automating AI research itself. The key test is whether the reported internal workflow can deliver repeatable results for outside researchers.
watch: The pretraining cost, development timeline, context capacity and agent capabilities are company-reported, not independent validation. Lor is in private beta, not broadly available. The announcement does not disclose a valuation. Earlier model and product announcements are context, not new launches in this funding announcement.

headline: NATCO Pharma Q2 profit falls 61% to Rs 202.6 crore as international formulations revenue contracts
body: NATCO Pharma reported Q2 FY27 consolidated profit after share of associate profit of Rs 202.6 crore, against Rs 517.9 crore a year earlier. Total revenue, including other income, fell to Rs 1,019.4 crore from Rs 1,463 crore. International formulations revenue, including profit share and subsidiaries, declined to Rs 668.4 crore from Rs 1,140.2 crore, while domestic formulations revenue rose to Rs 145.7 crore from Rs 105.4 crore. Company-defined EBITDA, which includes other income, fell to Rs 310 crore from Rs 679.2 crore; its margin declined to 30.4% from 46.4%.
why: Judgment: The international formulations decline outweighed growth in domestic formulations and other businesses. Revenue recovered from the preceding quarter, but associate-profit contribution helped reported profit, making the mix important to track.
watch: Total revenue and the stated EBITDA margin include other income; they are not revenue-from-operations measures. Q2 profit before associate contribution was Rs 173.4 crore, with Rs 29.2 crore of associate profit bringing the total to Rs 202.6 crore. Sequential total revenue rose from Rs 794.4 crore, but profit after associate contribution slipped from Rs 206.5 crore.

headline: York Space Systems records $749.7 million goodwill impairment as Q3 revenue falls 7%
body: York Space Systems reported Q3 revenue of $84.2 million, down 7% year on year, and a net loss of $807.4 million. The loss included a $749.7 million non-cash goodwill impairment, which York linked to difficulty estimating the timing and amount of future contract awards beyond 2026. Adjusted EBITDA was a $27.6 million loss, versus a $3.4 million loss a year earlier. Gross margin fell to 18%, down 400 basis points. York narrowed its full-year revenue outlook to $380 million-$400 million. September-end backlog was $581 million; cash and available revolving credit totaled $459 million.
why: Judgment: The impairment exposes uncertainty around future awards, while weaker revenue, gross margin and adjusted EBITDA show pressure beyond the non-cash accounting charge. Converting contract positions into funded work matters more than the larger opportunity pipeline.
watch: The impairment is non-cash, not a $749.7 million cash outflow. Adjusted EBITDA is non-GAAP. York says its $14.9 billion opportunity pipeline covers the next two years; it is not awarded backlog or guaranteed revenue. Its proposed Outlook Industries acquisition remains subject to approvals and closing conditions.

headline: Godrej Industries Q2 profit rises 131% to Rs 560 crore, including Rs 375 crore GCPL stake-sale gain

Consolidated profit before share of equity-accounted investees, exceptional items and tax fell to Rs 555.68 crore from Rs 686.83 crore. Chemicals revenue rose 26% to Rs 1,335 crore and segment PBIT rose 18% to Rs 114 crore.

The filing warns that changes in group holdings make periods not strictly comparable. Chemicals management expects the rest of the year to normalize without the recent demand-supply and inflation tailwinds.

The company identified data centers, utilities, metals and mining, and infrastructure among key demand areas.

watch: Figures use ABB India's continuing-business press-release basis, not total reported profit including discontinued operations. Orders are not revenue already recognized, and backlog does not guarantee future margins. ABB India follows a calendar financial year; this is the July-September quarter.

headline: Tata Motors PV posts about Rs 5,500 crore Q2 loss; JLR revises annual margin and cash-flow guidance
body: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 96,920 crore, up 34% year on year, but a net loss of about Rs 5,500 crore after roughly Rs 6,700 crore of exceptional items. The company identified employee-separation provisions and asset impairments as the main charges. Consolidated profit before tax and exceptional items was Rs 403 crore, while free cash outflow was about Rs 6,300 crore and net debt reached about Rs 50,800 crore. JLR revised full-year guidance to a 2-3% adjusted EBIT margin and approximately GBP 1.25 billion free cash outflow.
why: Judgment: The revenue recovery has not translated into cash generation. Exceptional costs and JLR's revised outlook matter more than the weak prior-year comparison alone.
watch: The company says year-on-year margin improvement mainly reflects recovery from last year's JLR cyber incident. Sequential margins were hurt by mix and commodity costs. JLR's guidance is a forecast, not an achieved result. These are passenger-vehicle and JLR results, not the separately listed commercial-vehicle company's October results.

headline: MUFG raises FY26 profit target to JPY 2.8 trillion and approves up to JPY 200 billion second-half buyback
body: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group raised its FY2026 parent-attributable net-income target by JPY 100 billion to JPY 2.8 trillion. First-half net income was JPY 1.6308 trillion, up JPY 337.9 billion year on year. MUFG also raised its annual dividend forecast to JPY 100 per common share, JPY 4 above its initial forecast, and resolved to repurchase up to JPY 200 billion of common stock in the second half. The full-year net operating profit target remained JPY 2.9 trillion.
why: Judgment: Higher expected profit supports a larger dividend forecast and another authorized capital-return program, but these remain future earnings and execution commitments.
watch: FY2026 ends in March 2027. The JPY 200 billion figure is the second-half repurchase ceiling, not purchases already completed; MUFG describes JPY 300 billion for the full year. The JPY 100 annual dividend is a forecast, not a payment already made. The net operating profit target was not raised.

headline: Eramet launches approximately EUR 500 million rights issue; French State commits about 64%
body: Eramet launched an approximately EUR 500 million gross rights issue on November 13, moving its previously announced funding plan to defined transaction terms. The issue will create 34,506,054 new shares, with six new shares available for every five subscription rights. France's APE, acting through a State-owned company, committed approximately EUR 322 million, or 64% of the issue; banks will underwrite the remainder. Net proceeds are intended to reduce debt, strengthen the balance sheet and support bank-covenant compliance.
why: Judgment: A dated, partly State-backed financing gives Eramet a defined balance-sheet repair route, but the capital has not yet been received.
watch: This is the launch of a previously announced plan, not a new EUR 500 million proposal or a completed raise. Rights trade November 16-25; subscriptions run November 18-27. Results are scheduled for December 2 and settlement for December 4. The public offer is limited to France, including specified overseas territories.

headline: Grasim Q2 revenue rises 26%, but owners' share posts Rs 234 crore loss after Canadian pulp-JV charge

Owners' share of reported profit turned to a Rs 234 crore loss from a Rs 595 crore profit; adjusted owners' profit before exceptional items fell 10% to Rs 536 crore. The presentation identifies a Rs 767 crore consolidated charge for impairment and estimated exposure in Canadian pulp JV AV Group NB. Separately, the board approved investment of up to C$91.8 million, approximately Rs 625 crore, in the JV's proposed rights issue, proportionate to Grasim's 45% holding.

Standalone PAT was Rs 2,306 crore, alongside Rs 4,017 crore dividend income and a separate Rs 825 crore JV charge. The rights-issue investment is approved, not completed. AVNB temporarily idled its Nackawic dissolving-pulp mill.

Profit for the period rose 39% to EUR 2.528 billion.

watch: Gross margin included a 190-basis-point benefit from the tariff-related items; excluding them, gross margin fell 70 basis points. Specialist Watchmakers still faced soft demand in China. Management expects continued macroeconomic and geopolitical volatility.

headline: Higurashi releases Haru-4B research model for simultaneous listening and speaking
body: Higurashi released Haru-4B as a pretrained research base model for full-duplex spoken dialogue, with weights on Hugging Face and code on GitHub. It is not a reliable source of facts and does not follow instructions like an assistant. The model processes incoming speech, outgoing speech and text together at 7.5 frames per second. The release includes PyTorch and MLX implementations, a web demo, a native macOS app and a vLLM-Omni plugin. The weights use an Apache 2.0 license.
why: Judgment: Open weights and local implementations give researchers a way to study interruptions, backchannels and turn-taking without a conventional listen-then-speak pipeline. This is a research foundation, not a ready-made reliable assistant.
watch: The model card says Haru-4B is not a reliable source of facts and does not follow instructions like an assistant. It can imitate a reference voice; the release says to use only voices users have rights to use. The developer's roughly 65 ms MacBook latency excludes audio framing, which can add up to 133 ms.

headline: Google and Samsung open Gemini eyewear preorders; US retail launch planned for December 10
body: Google announced preorders for Intelligent Eyewear made with Warby Parker, Gentle Monster and Samsung. watch: Google limits use to compatible adult Google accounts from the US and South Korea, with specified supported phones. Guided Vision and Aira require a compatible Android phone at launch. headline: VulcanForms agrees $500 million financing led by J.P. Morgan and Apollo funds for manufacturing expansion
body: VulcanForms said it reached an agreement for $500 million in financing led by J.P. Morgan and funds managed by Apollo. The company plans three new factories in addition to its three existing manufacturing sites. Its platform combines metal additive manufacturing, precision machining, automation and physical AI for components used across medical, consumer, aerospace, defense and other industrial markets.
why: Judgment: The financing targets expansion of US production capacity, rather than a software-only AI product. Factory construction and production delivery remain the test of whether the capital agreement translates into operating capacity.
watch: The release does not disclose valuation, financing instrument, drawdown terms, new-factory locations or opening dates. VulcanForms says it has secured multibillion-dollar commercial programs, but does not provide customer-by-customer contracts or a delivery schedule.

headline: Cerebras Q3 GAAP revenue reaches $210.8 million; non-GAAP core revenue $230.9 million as cloud inference grows
body: Cerebras reported Q3 GAAP revenue of $210.8 million, up 55% year on year, versus non-GAAP core revenue of $230.9 million, up 70%. GAAP gross margin was 20% and operating margin was negative 106%; core gross margin was 41% and core operating margin negative 14%. For Q4, the company forecasts core revenue of $310 million-$330 million and core operating margin between negative 1% and positive 1%.
why: Judgment: Cloud inference growth is driving a larger business, but the gap between GAAP and core measures makes the revenue definition important. Core measures add back customer-warrant amortization and exclude data-center pass-through revenue and costs; relevant profit measures also exclude stock compensation and other items.
watch: Cerebras says Oracle Cloud Infrastructure availability is planned for 2027 and identifies another new customer only as a top-three hyperscaler. It has secured 700 gross MW of data-center capacity for delivery by end-2027, not 700 MW already operating. FY2026 core revenue guidance is $940 million-$960 million.

headline: Cisco Q1 revenue rises 24% to $18.5 billion; raises FY27 outlook and hyperscaler AI revenue expectation to $9 billion
body: Cisco reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $18.5 billion, up 24% year on year, and GAAP net income of $4.6 billion, up 59%. GAAP EPS was $1.14; non-GAAP EPS was $1.40. Networking product revenue rose 43%, while services revenue grew 1%. Cisco raised its FY27 outlook to revenue of $74.8 billion-$75.8 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $5.47-$5.53. It also raised its expectation for FY27 hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue to $9 billion.
why: Judgment: The higher full-year outlook and hyperscaler revenue expectation offer a fresh test of networking demand linked to AI. Revenue growth was accompanied by operating-margin gains, but gross margin weakened.
watch: Non-GAAP operating margin was 37.8%, while non-GAAP gross margin fell to 65.6% from 68.1%. Q2 revenue guidance is $18.0 billion-$18.2 billion, below the reported Q1 level. The $9 billion hyperscaler figure is an annual revenue expectation, not orders already booked.
watch_next: Hyperscaler revenue delivery, networking growth and Q2 margins against the company outlook.
wrong_if: Hyperscaler demand falls short or weaker gross margins prevent delivery against the raised annual outlook.
likely_reaction: Positive: The raised outlook and hyperscaler expectation may support sentiment next session, tempered by gross-margin pressure and execution risk.

headline: Meta publishes MetaEncoder v1 for multimodal embeddings, retrieval and bounded decisions
body: The facebook organization on Hugging Face published MetaEncoder v1, with model files and a wrapper for encoding, retrieval and bounded decisions. The model card lists text, images, video frames and document-image inputs. It returns 6,656-dimensional normalized embeddings, can rank a corpus against a query, and answers yes/no, multiple-choice and score questions with probabilities. The card says one 80 GB GPU holds the model in bf16 and requires Transformers 5.15 or later.
why: Judgment: A single encoder can support both retrieval and bounded choices over multimodal inputs. Its probabilities should not be treated as automatically calibrated for every application: the model card provides a separate calibration method using labeled data.

headline: Wirex launches invite-only Navoka payment agent with separate account and card; messaging expansion remains planned
body: Wirex announced Navoka, an invitation-only payment agent with a dedicated IBAN, debit card and stablecoin wallet kept separate from the user's personal accounts. Wirex says users can instruct payments on Telegram or connect Navoka to ChatGPT, Claude or Grok; WhatsApp and iMessage support is planned. The company says card transactions are checked against user-set merchant, spending, daily and country limits, and actions outside those rules wait for approval.
why: Judgment: The launch applies separate payment accounts and transaction-level controls to agent commerce. The announcement establishes an invite-only product launch, not independent proof that its controls prevent every unwanted payment.
watch: Wirex says users can freeze the card and disconnect linked assistants, and payments record the governing rule and approval. General availability, country-specific eligibility and independent evidence of control effectiveness are not established by this release.

headline: Legence raises 2026 outlook after 85% Q3 revenue growth; Bowers acquisition accounts for part of the increase
body: Legence reported Q3 revenue of $1.311 billion, up 85.1% year on year. Excluding Bowers, its non-GAAP revenue growth was 39.5%. Net income attributable to Legence was $89.6 million versus a $0.6 million loss; non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA rose 99.3% to $177 million. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $4.87 billion-$4.91 billion from $4.70 billion-$4.80 billion, and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $610 million-$620 million from $565 million-$585 million. It also disclosed a $150 million share repurchase authorization, which does not require purchases.
why: Judgment: The raised outlook offers a fresh read on demand for building-system installation and fabrication. Legence attributed that segment's growth partly to data-center and technology customers, but the acquisition means headline revenue growth overstates growth excluding Bowers. Engineering and consulting revenue fell 5.8%.
watch: Backlog and awarded contracts totaled $5.90 billion, up 92.5%; this includes awarded work without signed formal contracts. Initial 2027 revenue guidance is $5.3 billion-$5.6 billion, with adjusted EBITDA of $690 million-$730 million. These are company forecasts, not booked revenue.

likely_reaction: Positive: The raised outlook and growth excluding Bowers may support sentiment next session, tempered by weaker consulting revenue and execution risk.

headline: Google starts Gemini 4 Hydrogen rollout across apps, Search and developer tools; Antigravity adds model orchestration
body: Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen for everyday coding and agentic workflows and said global rollout starts November 12 across developer, enterprise and consumer products. In the Gemini app, free users get Hydrogen through automatic model selection when appropriate, rather than an unrestricted manual choice. Google also introduced Orchestrator in Antigravity to switch between models such as Carbon and Hydrogen within one session. The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high by default, and xhigh.
why: Judgment: This broadens the Gemini 4 rollout beyond the previously announced Carbon model and adds automatic model switching for development workflows. Actual access and useful task completion remain the practical tests.

headline: Anthropic launches Claude for Manufacturing with 17 skills and four connectors; equipment control remains research
body: Anthropic launched a Claude for Manufacturing plugin for Team and Enterprise plans. Its 17 skills cover jobs such as drafting quotes, investigating failed inspections, diagnosing breakdowns and compiling production reports. Four connectors link Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365 and Oracle NetSuite. The skills are built to end with a person reviewing the work before it reaches a customer or supplier. The plugin does not operate equipment. Anthropic describes its separate Model Hardware Standard as a research preview.
why: Judgment: Anthropic is packaging Claude around plant-team workflows and existing business records, rather than offering autonomous equipment operation. The practical test is whether teams can use the connected records to produce work they can check and approve.
watch: Available on Team and Enterprise. The manufacturing Infor connector looks up records; a separate Infor plugin can make changes after buyer approval, within that buyer's permissions. Owning article dated November 12, 2026; no original publication time established.

headline: Nvidia says Jensen Huang resigns immediately; CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO
body: Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive officer and a board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while continuing as executive vice president and CFO. The board is starting a search for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates. Harvey C. Jones was appointed board chair. The board said it expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to continue without interruption.
why: Judgment: An immediate CEO and board departure is a material leadership change, distinct from earlier reports or speculation. Continuity of the product roadmap is the board's expectation, not an independently established outcome.

wrong_if: The transition disrupts execution or customer commitments despite the board's continuity expectations.

headline: Vodafone Idea Q2 loss widens to Rs 5,975 crore despite revenue and subscriber gains; capex more than doubles sequentially

headline: JD.com completes EUR 1.335 billion CECONOMY takeover purchase, acquiring 59.8% and starting consolidation
body: JD.com announced completion of its voluntary public takeover offer for CECONOMY, acquiring 59.8% of its share capital and voting rights for EUR 1.335 billion. headline: Intuitive Machines posts $269 million Q3 revenue and positive free cash flow; FY2026 outlook $920 million-$950 million

headline: Enovix halts smartphone system-level testing for current cells, shifts silicon-anode work to smart eyewear

It will not proceed with system-level field testing of those pre-AI-2 units and is concentrating silicon-anode development on smart eyewear. The company introduced FY2027 revenue guidance of $65 million-$85 million; nearly half the midpoint is already in backlog, according to management. Q3 revenue was $11.0 million, with a GAAP operating loss of $39.3 million. A 220-position reduction in early November cut approximately $8.5 million in annual costs. A $19 million expansion to double South Korean drone-battery capacity is expected online in Q2 2027.
why: Judgment: The strategic shift matters more than the quarterly revenue increase: smartphone system testing stops for the current cells while near-term resources move toward eyewear and Korean drone-battery operations.

headline: Manappuram Q2 profit rises 223% year on year to Rs 701 crore; gold-loan AUM nearly doubles

headline: Santander raises intended Brasil minority exchange-offer ratio by 5%; shareholder and regulatory approvals remain pending

Before dividend adjustments, holders would receive 0.4260 new Santander shares per Brasil unit or ADS, versus 0.4056 previously, and 0.2130 per common or preferred share, versus 0.2028. headline: Xero announces up to A$1 billion buyback and raises FY27 revenue outlook; Melio changes the comparison base

Xero raised FY27 revenue guidance to NZ$3.77 billion-NZ$3.83 billion from NZ$3.62 billion-NZ$3.73 billion; adjusted EBITDA guidance is now NZ$880 million-NZ$920 million, versus NZ$860 million-NZ$920 million.

headline: Siemens AG raises mid-term growth targets after record industrial profit; FY27 outlook excludes Healthineers
body: Siemens AG raised its mid-term comparable revenue-growth target to 7%-11% from 6%-9% and now targets double-digit EPS pre-PPA growth rather than high-single-digit growth. FY2026 revenue rose 8% on a comparable basis to EUR 83.4 billion; industrial-business profit rose 13% to EUR 13.3 billion, with margin of 16.3% versus 15.4%. Digital-business revenue grew 16% to EUR 10.9 billion. Group net income fell to EUR 9.5 billion from EUR 10.4 billion, with the prior year including a EUR 2.1 billion Innomotics disposal gain. For FY2027, Siemens expects 9%-11% comparable revenue growth and EPS pre-PPA of EUR 10.20-EUR 10.80, on a basis excluding Healthineers-related effects. Comparable FY26 EPS on that basis was EUR 9.27, not reported EPS pre-PPA of EUR 11.76.

headline: Naver Q3 operating profit falls 20.9% despite 10.7% revenue growth as AI investment rises

headline: Blackstone agrees to fund up to $1.5 billion of Pfizer obesity-drug development through 2028
body: Pfizer and Blackstone Life Sciences announced a co-funding agreement covering up to $1.5 billion of development costs through 2028 for berobenatide, an investigational monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions. Blackstone will be eligible for milestone-based payments tied to US approval of monthly injectable berobenatide monotherapy for chronic weight management and specified commercial sales milestones. Any payments earned would be spread over multiple years. Blackstone does not acquire rights or ownership in the drug, and Pfizer retains full operational control and decision-making over the program.
why: Judgment: External development funding gives Pfizer more financial room for its broader pipeline while preserving control of the obesity program. It also creates potential future milestone obligations, rather than transferring drug ownership.
watch: Up to $1.5 billion over time, not all paid upfront. Berobenatide remains investigational; this is a funding agreement, not an approval or new clinical readout.

headline: AeroVironment wins $405 million Middle East order for LOCUST X3 laser defense systems
body: AeroVironment announced a $405 million international direct commercial sales order for LOCUST X3 high-energy laser weapon systems, expanding counter-drone capabilities in the Middle East. The company did not name the customer, state the number of systems or give a delivery timetable in this release. LOCUST X3 is designed to counter Group 1 to 3 unmanned aircraft alongside radar, command-and-control and conventional weapons. AV intends to establish an in-country maintenance and sustainment depot for repair, technical support, training and lifecycle services. The depot is a plan, not a completed facility.
why: Judgment: A disclosed $405 million order gives a concrete commercial marker for laser-based counter-drone defense. AV argues that lasers can preserve more expensive missile interceptors, but its claimed engagement-cost advantage is not independently quantified in the release.
watch: Order award, not delivered systems or recognized revenue. Customer identity, system count and delivery schedule are not disclosed; the local support depot remains planned.

likely_reaction: Positive: The $405m order may support next-session sentiment, but delivery timing and conversion to revenue remain undisclosed.

headline: DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2 for cell-specific DNA research; commercial access remains private preview
body: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a DNA-sequence model for predicting variant effects in specific cell types and states. DeepMind says it is available via the AlphaGenome API and Colab tutorials for non-commercial research; commercial research remains in private preview. The model takes a million-letter DNA sequence plus a biological condition. DeepMind reports training on over 107 million cell profiles, conditioning on new single-cell data without retraining, and improved variant-effect recall on an immune-cell dataset. AlphaGenome 2 Skills for Antigravity are planned, not released. The model is research-only and has not been validated or approved for clinical or diagnostic use.
why: Judgment: Cell-specific predictions can help researchers prioritize which variants, genes and cell states to test experimentally. They are hypothesis-generation tools, not proof of disease causation or treatment effectiveness.
watch: Performance improvements are DeepMind-reported. Commercial use is private preview; research availability does not imply clinical validation or approval.
watch_next: Independent validation, commercial-preview access and the planned Antigravity Skills release.

headline: Runway releases Praxis-1 robot-policy weights and code under Apache 2.0
body: Runway released Praxis-1 robot-policy weights and inference and fine-tuning code under Apache 2.0, following its September introduction. It predicts video and robot actions together. Public model pages expose single-arm DROID and bimanual YAM checkpoints, each with about 54.4 GB of weights. Their documented inference path needs one 80 GB GPU; the quick start specifies Python 3.12 and CUDA 13.0. Full fine-tuning and LoRA are documented. Separate frozen video-autoencoder and text-encoder dependencies retain their own licenses.
why: Judgment: Downloadable policies and adaptation code let robotics teams test a video-action model locally. Compute and embodiment requirements still limit use; broad hardware claims are not proof of unchanged operation on any robot.
watch: Benchmark and broad hardware claims are Runway-reported. The documented DROID/YAM checkpoints require one 80 GB GPU; separate frozen dependencies have their own licenses.

headline: Google Labs introduces Tabletop for AI-built group planning spaces, limited to US adults via waitlist
body: Google Labs introduced Tabletop, an experiment for real-time group collaboration. Users can add links, files and ideas, then prompt @tabletop or choose a template to generate interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets. An invite link lets other people join and use the space at the same time. Google says access is rolling out in the US for people aged 18 and over through a waitlist. This is not a global launch or general availability for every user.
why: Judgment: Tabletop puts generated interactive tools inside a shared group workspace rather than leaving each person with a private AI response. The initial scope is everyday planning, with access still restricted.
watch: Google describes Tabletop as a Labs experiment. Access is waitlisted, US-only and restricted to adults; broader availability is not announced.
watch_next: Waitlist access, real-world collaboration reliability and any expansion beyond US adults.

headline: AWS makes local AWS Emulator generally available, with service-fidelity and IAM limits
body: AWS made its Rust-based local AWS Emulator generally available for development and testing with AWS CLI and SDK workflows. AWS says autonomous agents wrote the code, with fidelity tests and release gates. It is not a production or security-testing substitute: IAM and resource-policy behavior differ from AWS, each instance uses one account without cross-account or cross-Region behavior, and fidelity varies by service. Missing operations return HTTP 501. Linux packages are available; macOS and Windows use a locally built Docker image.
why: Judgment: A local AWS-compatible target can shorten coding-agent test loops. Teams still need cloud integration and security tests because local success does not establish matching AWS behavior.
watch: AWS reports the agent-built development process. Fidelity varies by service; IAM behavior is not equivalent to AWS. Default usage/error telemetry can be disabled.
watch_next: Per-service fidelity scores, missing-operation fixes and adoption in developer and CI workflows.
wrong_if: Local tests frequently pass despite materially different behavior on real AWS for the workflows teams need.

headline: ElevenLabs opens ElevenAI early access; agent memory, routines and model fine-tuning remain forthcoming

Separate ElevenAgents additions remain staged: Memory and Routines are forthcoming, Interaction Engine was previewed, and customer-specific fine-tuning of selected open-source language models and ElevenLabs voice models is planned for coming months. watch: Early access is not general availability. Business-use and consent restrictions apply. Memory, Routines, Interaction Engine and fine-tuning have different forthcoming or preview states.

headline: Google starts global Gemini Live rollout on Apple CarPlay, with inbox and calendar conversations
body: Google is rolling out Gemini Live on Apple CarPlay globally to iOS users across supported languages. Users can start or resume conversations, ask about Gmail and Google Calendar, and continue on iPhone after parking. Setup needs the latest Gemini iPhone app, microphone permission and prior use of Live on the phone. Daily Brief needs separate setup; it and some personalization features are unavailable to under-18s and in the EEA and Nigeria. This is a rollout, not confirmation every account has access.

headline: Simon Willison releases LLM 0.37.2 to fix two custom-endpoint OpenAI API-key disclosure bugs
body: Simon Willison released LLM 0.37.2, patching two moderate-severity bugs that could send a configured OpenAI API key to a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint. One affected versions from 0.6 up to but excluding 0.37.2; the other from 0.32a2 up to but excluding 0.37.2. Both depend on specific endpoint and key settings. The owning release and advisories identify 0.37.2 as patched. They do not establish universal exposure or active exploitation.
why: Judgment: The patch addresses unintended credential disclosure across provider trust boundaries. Exposure depends on the custom-endpoint configuration, not simply having LLM installed.
watch: Both advisories are rated moderate and depend on specific custom-endpoint/key settings. The sources do not establish active exploitation or universal exposure.
watch_next: Advisory updates, downstream package adoption and any confirmed impact from affected configurations.
wrong_if: The release does not fully prevent unintended credential fallback in the documented custom-endpoint paths.

headline: Google introduces Gemini Decisions API for bounded multimodal choices; Cloud support is still planned
body: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API in Google AI Studio, powered by Gemini Decision 1. It scores up to 1,000 independent questions against shared multimodal input of up to 256K tokens, returning probabilities and confidence scores. It supports yes/no, multiple-choice and rubric scoring. Google reports 150-250ms end-to-end latency for contexts up to 16K tokens, nearly flat from one to 100 questions in its tests, not at the maximum limits. Google Cloud support is coming soon; ecosystem integrations are rolling out.
why: Judgment: A scoring endpoint could replace full text generation for routing and policy checks. Confidence scores can help flag uncertain cases, but do not make decisions error-free.
watch: Latency and calibration claims are Google-reported, not independently verified. The stated latency test uses up to 16K context, not the 256K maximum.
watch_next: Independent latency and calibration tests at larger contexts, integration availability and Google Cloud rollout.
wrong_if: Scores are poorly calibrated or practical workloads lose the claimed latency advantage and need costly fallback calls.

headline: Triveni Turbine Q2 profit falls 41.7% as exports and margins weaken; order booking reaches a record

headline: Google releases stable A2UI 1.0 for agent interfaces; Jetpack Compose and Gemini upgrades are pending
body: Google released A2UI 1.0, the first stable version of its open protocol for agent-generated interfaces. Agents describe screens as data; host apps render registered native components instead of arbitrary generated UI code. Version 1.0 adds bidirectional function calls, accessibility support and extension metadata, with Python, TypeScript and Dart agent SDKs. Web, Flutter and SwiftUI renderers are available. Jetpack Compose and Gemini still support 0.9.1, with 1.0 upgrades pending. ByteDance Lynx supports 0.9 and is adapting to 1.0. Not every renderer or host has upgraded.
why: Judgment: A stable protocol gives developers a shared format for interactive forms and review screens. Native rendering does not remove host-version gaps or the need to test integrations.
watch: The protocol is stable, but Jetpack Compose and Gemini are not yet on 1.0. Security and latency benefits are design claims, not guarantees. ByteDance Lynx remains on0.9, adapting to1.0. Team adoption examples do not mean all deployments are on1.0.

headline: Fractile raises $720 million at $7 billion valuation with UK state backing for AI chips
body: Fractile raised $720 million at a $7 billion post-money valuation, participating investor Balderton announced on November 11. Thrive, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint co-led the round. The UK government confirmed Sovereign AI and British Business Bank backing for the Series C, describing the round as worth over £500 million and the valuation as over £5 billion. Individual state contributions were not disclosed. Fractile is developing AI chips and systems. This funding is not evidence of commercial shipments or independently validated performance.
why: Judgment: The private round and state participation give a UK AI hardware developer more capital. Commercial deployment, software support and workload economics remain to be demonstrated.
watch: Individual state contributions were not disclosed. This card reports funding, not validated chip performance or commercial shipments. Balderton gives a Nov11 date without an hour; the precise clock is the government announcement.
